competency: State the principles of vegetable crop management and calculate the profit of a vegetable crop.

en.text: Choosing a site means checking land-use history, soil properties and pollution, the availability and quality of water, and effects of nearby crops. Gentle slopes are suitable; steep slopes speed up erosion, so terraces or other conservation works may be needed first. Sustainability is helped by accurate records of yield, varieties, fertilizer, pesticides, irrigation and other inputs, soil analysis, techniques, and market information such as sales, demand and prices.

ideas.name: Planting material, integrated crop management and water

en.text: Good planting material is adapted to local conditions, resistant to pests and diseases, meets consumer quality demand and is planted at the right time; check seed, bulb and tuber quality. Integrated crop management uses diverse crop rotations, avoids over-dependence on chemicals, adds crop residues or compost, and gives balanced nutrients based on soil analysis and nutrients from organic matter. Water should be used economically, matched to crop need, checked for quality, and protected from fertilizer contamination.

en.text: Marketing is one of the most important factors for success, and it starts before production: choosing crops and varieties and planning how produce reaches consumers at an acceptable profit. All costs (seed, fertilizer, pesticides, labour, harvest, postharvest handling, marketing) must be counted. Gross income = yield × price, and net profit = gross income − costs. In the book's example, 4,500 kg of tomato at 25 birr/kg gives 112,500 birr; minus 51,300 birr costs, the profit is 61,200 birr per hectare per cropping season.

notes.text: p.17: the tomato example labels the result "Net profit per month", but 61,200 birr is per cropping season (the book's own last line says so). Taught as per season; about 15,300 birr per month if a season lasts 4 months. Also, 45 q/ha is a low tomato yield; the example is indicative, as the book says.

p.15: "tubers, bulbs and tubers" should be "seeds, bulbs and tubers". "Organic fertilizers and soil analysis show soil nutrient content" is garbled: soil (and manure) analysis shows nutrient content so fertilizer rates can be adjusted.
Added: the profit slider, the enterprise-steps order item, cost per kg, profit per month and the price-fall challenge.
